title: Section invariant
statement:
Use the purity coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions]: the global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. The finite coefficient stage is $\Lambda=A$; the stages $\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use the coefficient constructions specified in those conventions. Let $B,V$ be finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $g:V\to B$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type, and let $s:B\to V$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $g\circ s=\mathrm{id}_B$.

On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], let $Rg^!$ be the constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], let $Ls^*$ and $\otimes^L_\Lambda$ be the derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom, def-weil-derived-tensor], and let $\Lambda_T$ denote the coefficient tensor unit on a scheme $T$: the constant sheaf $A_T$ at finite level, the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] at integral level, and its rationalized or common-stage image at the field levels [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $\omega_g:=Rg^!\Lambda_B$. Define the *section invariant* by the actual derived pullback
$$
 C(g,s):=Ls^*\omega_g=Ls^*Rg^!\Lambda_B.
$$
It is tensor-invertible in $D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]: there is $Q\in D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$ with $C(g,s)\otimes^L_\Lambda Q\simeq\Lambda_B\simeq Q\otimes^L_\Lambda C(g,s)$. Thus it is an object of $\operatorname{Pic}(D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda))$, the groupoid whose objects are tensor-invertible objects and whose arrows are their isomorphisms. No choice of an orientation or of an isomorphism to a Tate twist is part of this definition.

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant] the relative-dimension loci $V_d$ of $g$ are open and closed. They cover the quasi-compact finite-type $k$-scheme $V$, so only finitely many are nonempty. By [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition], each $g_d:V_d\to B$ is smooth, and it has pure relative dimension $d$ by the definition of $V_d$. It is separated and of finite type: its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $g$, and a clopen subset of each quasi-compact inverse image of an affine open of $B$ is quasi-compact. Local finite-type conditions restrict to open subschemes. Thus the pure-dimensional theorem can be applied to every $g_d$, even though the dimension of $g$ need not be constant.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] to the finite cover $(V_d)_d$. It identifies the constructible finite-Tor category, its tensor and its unit with the product of the corresponding categories on the pieces. Apply [lem-pur-finite-clopen-exceptional-restriction] with $L=\Lambda_B$ to identify the component of $\omega_g$ with $\omega_{g_d}$ at every coefficient stage. Its system-level clause supplies the integral comparison; there is no passage from unrelated levelwise isomorphisms to a coherent tower. These statements also cover empty $V$.

source.place: Definition def-pur-section-invariant, formula and final invertibility assertion; expanded well-definedness

proof.text: Apply the invertibility clause of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] to each $g_d$ of step 1. Its schemes and coefficients are in the same purity conventions, and each $g_d$ is smooth separated with the single relative dimension $d$ required by that theorem. Choose an inverse $P_d$ of $\omega_{g_d}$ in the stated finite-Tor category. The finite product construction of step 2 gives a genuine object $P$ with these components, and the componentwise inverse isomorphisms give $\omega_g\otimes^L_\Lambda P\simeq\Lambda_V\simeq P\otimes^L_\Lambda\omega_g$. Thus $\omega_g$ and its inverse belong to $D^b_{ctf}(V,\Lambda)$. No implication from geometric smoothness to cohomological smoothness is taken from the definition of cohomological smoothness; the required mathematical input is the theorem just cited.

source.place: Definition def-pur-section-invariant, formula and final invertibility assertion; expanded well-definedness

proof.text: Define $C(g,s)=Ls^*\omega_g$ by the actual derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and put $Q=Ls^*P$. The data of $C(g,s)$ are therefore fixed by a construction. The closed immersion $s$ is proper, hence separated and of finite type, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. At finite coefficients apply [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] to each $F\in\{\omega_g,P\}$: the source and target schemes are finite type over $k$ and $F$ is bounded constructible with a finite Tor interval by step 3. It follows that both $Ls^*F$ belong to $D^b_{ctf}(B,A)$, with their original Tor bounds.

source.place: Definition def-pur-section-invariant, formula and final invertibility assertion; expanded well-definedness

proof.text: At integral coefficients [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], clause 1, gives $Ls^*F\in D^b_c(B,\mathcal O_E)$ and identifies its $j$-th reduction with $Ls_j^*F_j$, where $F_j=F\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,j}$. By [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the $F_j$ have one Tor interval $[a_F,b_F]$ independent of $j$. Apply [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] at every $j$: it preserves exactly that interval, so all reductions of $Ls^*F$ satisfy the required common bound. The same definition therefore puts $Ls^*F$ in $D^b_{ctf}(B,\mathcal O_E)$. At the rational stage pullback is integral pullback on representatives; at the algebraically closed stage it is represented at a finite coefficient field [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. These operations preserve bounded constructibility, and at both field stages $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Apply this to both choices of $F$.

source.place: Definition def-pur-section-invariant, formula and final invertibility assertion; expanded well-definedness

proof.text: The pullback of the unit is the unit. At finite level [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] computes exact inverse image of the constant sheaf, giving $Ls^*\Lambda_V\simeq\Lambda_B$. At integral level that construction and [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible], clause 2, compute this pullback as $R\varprojlim_j\operatorname{Res}_j(A_{E,j})_B\simeq\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,B}$. Indeed clause 2 identifies all finite reductions of the completed unit with the finite constant units, and its derived completeness identifies the completed unit with this derived limit. At field levels apply rationalization to this integral isomorphism and then represent it at a common finite stage, as specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

proof.text:
Apply $Ls^*$ to the two inverse isomorphisms in step 3. The tensor comparison of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], applied to $(\omega_g,P)$ and $(P,\omega_g)$, and step 6 give
$$
 C(g,s)\otimes^L_\Lambda Q\simeq Ls^*(\omega_g\otimes^L_\Lambda P)\simeq\Lambda_B,
 \qquad Q\otimes^L_\Lambda C(g,s)\simeq\Lambda_B.
$$
The cited comparison includes the compatible finite-reduction construction of the integral map and its rationalized and common-stage images. At finite level it is stated in the ambient derived category, so its use does not presume tensor closure for arbitrary bounded constructible inputs. Steps 4 and 5 place the factors in $D^b_{ctf}(B,\Lambda)$; the displayed isomorphisms exhibit the claimed inverse there. Hence the actual pullback $C(g,s)$ is an object of its Picard groupoid, with no orientation chosen.

lean.statement: def sectionInvariantFinite (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {V B : Scheme.{u}} (g : V ⟶ B) [Smooth g] [IsSeparated g] [QuasiCompact g] (aB : B ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType aB] [QuasiCompact aB] (s : B ⟶ V) [IsClosedImmersion s] (hs : s ≫ g = 𝟙 B) : proEtaleDerivedCategory B P.Ring
lean.note: Section 1(B): importing the recorded PuritySectionInvariant mixes the retired pro-etale UpperLowerStar.Iso with FiniteCoefficient.UpperLowerStar.Iso and fails with duplicate upperStarIsoLowerStarInv. Its fixed-scalar section invariant also does not directly inhabit the intrinsic finiteTorConstructible category. This replacement uses the canonical intrinsic coefficient realization, the published finite exceptional functor and exact derived pullback. sectionInvariantFinite obtains compactifiability from the source finite-type hypotheses; no ambient exceptional-adjoint admissibility or orientation is added. The finite coefficient stage is stated here; other stages remain the specified transports of def-pur-conventions.
